content:
maria: Heads-up — saw double-crediting around midnight for ~30 tenants. Looks like two finalizers claimed the same epoch window. Starting thread to flush out options.

josh: I noticed anomalies too. Logs show two claims within 2s: claim_id=abc123 and claim_id=def456 for window=2026-03-20T00:00Z.

sam: Isn't the lease supposed to prevent that? We use short TTL leases on finalizers.

maria: Right, but we lowered TTL to speed finalization. If runner restarts during claim+commit, second runner can win the final commit path.

anna: Quick brainstorm of options:
- central lease manager (etcd/consensus)
- append-only commit log + idempotent finalizer (finalized marker per-window)
- optimistic local claim + leader election on conflict

josh: Centralized lease is simplest to reason about but adds ops burden and single point of failure unless we run HA etcd. Also latency for every claim.

sam: Commit-log approach: finalizer writes intent then takes ownership by writing a "finalized" event. Readers consult the log as source of truth. More durable but requires backfill tooling to reconcile partial intents.

maria: Example contract (rough):
```http
POST /finalizer/intent
{ "window_id": "2026-03-20T00:00Z", "runner_id": "maria-1", "intent_id": "uuid-1", "seq": 102 }
// then
POST /finalizer/commit
{ "window_id": "2026-03-20T00:00Z", "intent_id": "uuid-1", "finalized_at": "..." }
```
If commit exists, other intents for same window should be ignored.

anna: That gives us an immutable source of truth. But GC and tombstone design matter — we need TTL for intents, and a safe compaction window for finalized markers.

josh: Tradeoffs:
- commit-log: stronger correctness, higher storage & backfill complexity
- central-lease: lower storage, simpler runtime, but harder to scale cross-region

sam: What about hybrid: optimistic local lease + push intent to commit-log as a race resolution step. If commit-log already has a finalized marker, the local finalizer aborts and replays nothing. That minimizes pressure on the log (only winners write commit).

maria: I like hybrid. Steps: 1) try local ephemeral lease; 2) do work; 3) write commit record; 4) finalizer idempotent on commit record existence. If two finish simultaneously, commit-log decides winner by first-write semantics.

josh: Need to ensure first-write is strictly ordered. Use commit log with compare-and-set on window key or a durable append with sequence numbers. If using append, ensure consumers check the latest finalized sequence.

anna: Also add monitoring: alert on >0.1% duplicate credits in a day, and a dedicated reconciliation job that scans recent windows for multiple finalizers.

ops-bot: deploy:monitoring created alert: "metering.duplicates.rate" threshold=0.001/day (owner=eng-platform).

sam: Implementation spikes: I'll prototype optimistic lease + CAS commit in the log. Need to measure latency and write amplification.

maria: I'll open an RFC that lays out hybrid flow, GC policy, and failure scenarios (runner OOM, network partition, clock skew).

josh: I'll run a small perf test comparing etcd lease vs commit-log CAS under load (~1000 windows/min).

anna: TL;DR consensus: try hybrid (optimistic lease + commit-log as source-of-truth). Spike owners: sam (prototype), josh (perf), maria (RFC + reconciliation runbook).

maria: Action items: will open RFC and link the spike issues. tagging @here for visibility :eyes:

josh: ack. I'll add perf test infra to the benchmarking repo and mock late-heartbeat scenarios.

sam: ack — will prototype by EOW.

maria: thanks all. We'll reconvene after spikes.
